job.title: Senior Contracts Advisor
job.description:
Senior Contracts Advisor

Brisbane Based | Long-term opportunity | ASAP Start

An exciting opportunity is available for an experienced Senior Contracts Advisor to join a well-established mining operation and play a key role within the Procurement & Supply Chain team.
Reporting to the Logistics & Contracts Manager, this is a senior, hands-on position responsible for leading the sourcing, negotiation, formation and execution of high-value contracts across maintenance, mining, civil works, logistics, capital equipment and operational services.

We're looking for someone who thrives on negotiating commercial outcomes, building strong relationships and influencing stakeholders at all levels. The successful candidate will be a confident communicator who can work effectively with operational teams, suppliers, contractors and senior leadership to achieve the best outcomes for the business.

About the Role
Key responsibilities include:
  • Lead end-to-end sourcing, tendering, negotiation and contract award activities.
  • Negotiate commercial and contractual terms to achieve best-value outcomes while effectively managing risk.
  • Manage complex, high-value and strategically important contracts across a diverse portfolio.
  • Prepare, review and finalise contract documentation, schedules and commercial correspondence.
  • Lead tender evaluations and prepare recommendations for contract award.
  • Manage commercial and contractual risk through well-structured contract terms and conditions.
  • Support contract owners with scope development, variations, contractor performance and dispute resolution.
  • Develop and improve contract templates, standards and contracting frameworks.
  • Build strong working relationships with internal stakeholders, suppliers, contractors and service providers.
  • Mentor and support junior contracts and procurement team members.
  • Ensure compliance with procurement governance, policies, delegations and contractual obligations.
About You
To be successful in this role, you'll bring:
  • Extensive experience in contract management, procurement or commercial roles within mining, resources, construction, civil or heavy industry environments.
  • Demonstrated experience negotiating and managing complex, high-value contracts.
  • Strong commercial acumen and a sound understanding of contract law principles and commercial risk allocation.
  • Exceptional stakeholder engagement skills, with the ability to build relationships and influence outcomes across operational, commercial and leadership teams.
  • Proven ability to negotiate commercially favourable outcomes while maintaining strong supplier and contractor relationships.
  • Experience leading tender processes, contract awards and supplier negotiations.
  • Strong communication skills and the confidence to engage with stakeholders at all levels.
  • Experience managing contractor performance, variations and commercial issues.
  • Ability to work autonomously while collaborating effectively across multiple business functions.
  • Proficiency with ERP systems and Microsoft Office, particularly Excel.
Highly Regarded
  • Mining, resources or heavy industry experience.
  • Experience managing maintenance, mining services, civil works or major project contracts.
  • Exposure to Australian Standard contracts (AS4000, AS2124, AS4902, AS4906).
  • Professional qualifications such as CIPS, WorldCC/IACCM or similar.
  • Experience supporting operational and capital project environments.
  • Experience within underground mining operations.
What's on Offer?
  • Brisbane-based opportunity.
  • Long-term opportunity.
  • ASAP start available.
  • Opportunity to work within a well-established mining operation.
  • Diverse portfolio of high-value contracts across operations and projects.
  • Senior stakeholder-facing role with genuine influence across the business.
  • Opportunity to lead negotiations and drive commercial outcomes.
  • Collaborative and supportive team environment.
Apply Now

If you're a commercially minded contracts professional who enjoys negotiating outcomes, working closely with contractors and suppliers, and building strong relationships with stakeholders, we'd love to hear from you.
This is an opportunity to play a key role in a high-performing team where your commercial expertise, negotiation skills and ability to influence people will have a direct impact on business success.

job.title: Internal Audit
job.description:
Chandler Macleod is recruiting on behalf of our Federal Government client for an experienced Audit and Assurance Officer to join their Governance team in Albury NSW, Griffith NSW,  Canberra ACT, Goondiwindi QLD, Mildura VIC, Adelaide SA , Murray Bridge SA. This is a 12 month, full time labour hire contract.
This is an excellent opportunity for a governance, audit, risk, or assurance professional to contribute to the delivery of effective governance frameworks, organisational resilience, risk management, and continuous improvement initiatives within a high-profile Commonwealth agency.

About the Role
The Audit and Assurance Officer plays a key role in supporting the agency's governance, audit, assurance, risk management, and business continuity functions.
Working closely with internal stakeholders, service providers, and governance committees, you will coordinate internal audits, monitor audit recommendations, support risk and assurance activities, and contribute to the ongoing improvement of governance and risk frameworks. You will also assist in strengthening organisational resilience through the management and coordination of business continuity planning and testing activities.

Key Responsibilities
As the Audit and Assurance Officer, you will:
  • Manage relationships and contracts with internal audit service providers, ensuring accountability and delivery against agreed milestones.
  • Coordinate the delivery of internal audits in accordance with the Annual Internal Audit Plan.
  • Liaise with stakeholders, facilitate information gathering, track audit progress, and support audit activities from commencement through to completion.
  • Maintain audit recommendation registers and monitor the implementation, reporting, escalation, and closure of management actions.
  • Prepare high-quality reports, briefings, and committee papers relating to audit, assurance, risk management, and business continuity matters.
  • Contribute to the continuous improvement of governance, audit, assurance, and risk management frameworks.
  • Coordinate quality assurance activities and support annual assessments of internal audit service effectiveness.
  • Support the effective operation of governance and oversight committees, including member onboarding and administrative coordination.
  • Coordinate external reviews, assurance activities, compliance assessments, and risk workshops.
  • Manage and maintain business continuity arrangements, including planning, testing exercises, resilience initiatives, and monitoring improvement actions.
  • Provide specialist advice on governance, audit, assurance, risk, and business continuity matters across the organisation.
About You
To be successful in this role, you will have demonstrated experience in governance, audit, assurance, risk management, compliance, or related fields within a government or highly regulated environment.

You will bring:
Audit, Risk & Assurance Expertise
  • Experience coordinating internal audit programs and assurance activities.
  • Strong understanding of governance, risk management, and control frameworks.
  • Knowledge of Australian Government audit, risk, and assurance principles.
  • Experience managing audit findings, recommendations, and reporting processes.
  • Understanding of business continuity planning and organisational resilience practices.
Strategic Thinking & Analysis
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills.
  • Ability to interpret complex information, identify emerging trends, and recommend practical improvements.
  • Experience contributing to strategic planning and assurance priorities.
  • Understanding of performance metrics, data analysis, and reporting.
Communication & Stakeholder Engagement
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
  • Experience preparing executive-level reports, briefing papers, and committee documentation.
  • Ability to influence, negotiate, and build credibility with senior stakeholders.
  • Strong relationship management and contract management capabilities.
Personal Effectiveness
  • Ability to work independently while collaborating effectively across geographically dispersed teams.
  • Strong organisational skills with the ability to manage competing priorities and meet deadlines.
  • High attention to detail and commitment to quality outcomes.
  • Sound judgement and the ability to provide trusted advice on complex governance and assurance matters.
 
Apply Now
If you are an experienced audit, assurance, governance, or risk professional looking for your next Federal Government opportunity, we encourage you to apply. – Aparna Garg Aparna.garg@chandlermacleod.com

At Chandler Macleod, we are committed to fostering a diverse workforce where everyone is welcome. We encourage applications from Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples, women, neurodiverse, people living with a disability and the LGBTIQA+ community.

You can read more about our commitment to diversity and inclusion at https://www.chandlermacleod.com/diversity-and-inclusion.

job.title: Mechanical Fitter
job.description:
Mechanical Fitter – Defence | $69–$71/hr + Penalties | Casual project to July 2027 | Mid-January Start

Chandler Macleod is seeking experienced Mechanical Fitters for an upcoming start in January on a major defence program based in Osborne. If you’re hands-on, safety-focused and confident working to high compliance standards, this is a great opportunity for project work through to July 2027 (with potential for further extension).
 
Why you’ll want this role
  • Top market rate: $69–$71 per hour + penalties
  • Casual project through to July 2027
  • Work on a high-profile defence project in a structured, safety-first environment
  • Free onsite parking
 
The role
You’ll be completing mechanical assembly and install work across a high-compliance site, including:
  • Mechanical assembly, fit-out and installation of equipment and components
  • Installation, overhaul and strip/rebuild of mechanical equipment
  • Planned and reactive maintenance and repairs to keep equipment performing safely and reliably
  • Reading and working from technical drawings, procedures and specifications (with a strong quality focus)
  • Testing and commissioning activities as required
  • Working closely with other trades, supervisors and QA to deliver safe, on-time outcomes in a structured environment
 
 
Essential requirements (must have)
To be considered, you will need:
  • Australian Citizenship
  • Trade Certificate (Mechanical Engineering / Mechanical Fitting)
  • National Police Clearance issued within the last 3 months
  • Confined Space (refreshed within the last 2 years)
  • Working at Heights + EWP
  • Proven mechanical assembly / installation experience in defence or heavy industrial
  • Current driver’s licence + reliable vehicle
 
Desirable
  • Hepatitis A & B vaccinations
  • Basic computer skills (job tracking, checklists, basic systems)
 
Security / site access
Successful candidates will be required to apply for a Naval Shipbuilding and Sustainment Identification Card (NSSIC) following interview.
 
How to apply
Click APPLY NOW to submit your resume. If you match the requirements and are available for a mid-January start, our team will contact you after review.

job.title: Customer Service
job.description:
Join a Global Logistics Leader in an ongoing temp role!
We’re looking for a motivated, customer-focused professional to join the depot team of a leading international logistics company.
Working at the heart of the operation, you’ll help ensure deliveries stay on track and customers receive the service they expect. You’ll be responsible for managing missed and delayed deliveries, coordinating rescheduled consignments, and liaising directly with customers to resolve delivery issues.

In this role, you’ll:
  • Coordinate and reschedule missed or delayed deliveries
  • Liaise with customers to arrange suitable delivery times
  • Investigate delivery issues and find practical solutions
  • Work closely with drivers, depot teams and internal departments
  • Update delivery information and maintain accurate records
  • Handle customer enquiries professionally and efficiently
  • Help keep the depot operation running smoothly and on schedule
What we’re looking for:
  • Excellent communication and customer service skills
  • Strong organisation and attention to detail
  • The ability to stay calm and solution-focused under pressure
  • Confidence dealing with customers and internal teams
  • Good computer and administrative skills
  • Previous experience in logistics, transport, warehousing or customer service is advantageous
Why join us?
This is an opportunity to work within a fast-paced, international logistics environment where every day brings new challenges. You’ll play an important role in connecting customers, drivers and depot operations — making sure problems are resolved and deliveries get where they need to go.

If you’re organised, approachable and enjoy solving problems, we’d love to hear from you.
Please email talia.moussa@chandlermacleod.com if you have any questions!

job.title: Warehousing / Production & Admin Assistant
job.description:
Warehousing/Production & Administration Assistant
AusPac Ingredients
Tamworth, Tamworth & North West NSW

Full-time, permanent

About The Role CCD Animal Health and AusPac Ingredients are seeking to appoint a full-time team member to assist our warehousing/production and customer service teams. This is an exciting opportunity requiring an organised and punctual candidate.

Reporting to the Business Services Manager, our new Warehousing/Administration Assistant's key responsibilities will be:

  • Picking and packing orders
  • General warehousing duties
  • Processing customer orders
  • Arranging transport of outward orders
  • Providing excellent customer service
About You Our ideal candidate will have strong attention to detail, experience in a warehousing and production environment, skills in customer service, and be able to work as part of an efficient and effective team. They will maintain a high level of professional communication with all stakeholders and manage their workload effectively in the face of competing priorities.

Applicants must have:
  • Experience in warehousing and production
  • Experience in customer service
  • The ability to work both in teams and autonomously, whilst communicating information effectively to colleagues
  • Experience working with Microsoft Office Suite
  • Outstanding interpersonal skills
  • Excellent verbal and written communication skills
  • Resilience and the ability to work with competing priorities, whilst maintaining a high attention to detail
  • Ability to be flexible in high-pressure scenarios, and able to adapt quickly and efficiently to change
  • Ability to complete repetitive data entry work with a high level of accuracy
  • Experience with accounting software such as MYOB Acumatica preferable
About Us AusPac is a business founded with the purpose of enabling excellence for our customers and internal stakeholders. We have a commitment to industry improvement, product quality and animal performance.

With a strong focus on meeting customer expectations for quality and service, we have the logistics and administrative capabilities to ensure these expectations are met.

CCD Animal Health is a leading distributor of quality veterinary pharmaceuticals and has an extensive sales, customer service and distribution network covering all regions of Australia. We are a quality focused supplier to the animal agriculture sector.

AusPac holds FAMI-QS accreditation, an all-encompassing management system for the feed industry, and CCD Animal Health holds an APVMA licence. We provide a level of assurance that the products we deliver are of the highest standard.

We are a business that promotes diversity, and a genuine focus on personal development to help build your capabilities and career. We also offer discounts at over 500 retailers through our reward and recognition platform as well as health and wellness initiatives.

Best of all, CCD Animal Health and AusPac Ingredients is a great place to work, where you can bring your authentic self!

job.title: Director Budgets and Reporting
job.description:
Chandler Macleod is recruiting on behalf of our client for an exceptional leadership opportunity within a high-profile Federal Government agency delivering one of Australia's most significant long-term capability programs.

This is a unique opportunity for an experienced finance leader to influence strategic decision-making, lead complex budget initiatives, and contribute to a nationally significant program that will shape Australia's future for decades to come.

About the Role Reporting directly to the Chief Financial Officer, the EL2 Director Budgets and Reporting will provide strategic leadership across budgeting, forecasting, financial reporting and financial management activities.

You will be responsible for driving financial sustainability, delivering high-quality budget outcomes, providing trusted advice to senior executives and leading a team responsible for the development and management of internal and external budget processes.

This is a critical leadership position for a forward-thinking finance professional who thrives in a dynamic environment and enjoys influencing strategic outcomes at the highest levels.

Key Responsibilities
  • Lead the development and implementation of budget management strategies and financial plans
  • Provide strategic financial advice, analysis and insights to executive stakeholders
  • Oversee internal and external budget processes, reporting and forecasting activities
  • Deliver accurate and timely financial reporting to senior leadership and governance committees
  • Identify, manage and mitigate budget risks while ensuring compliance and financial integrity
  • Enable effective financial business partnering across the organisation
  • Drive continuous improvement initiatives across budgeting and reporting functions
  • Lead, mentor and develop a high-performing team to achieve financial and operational outcomes
About You: 
You will demonstrate:
  • Extensive experience in budget management, forecasting and financial reporting
  • Strong strategic thinking and the ability to develop and implement financial strategies
  • Experience providing high-level financial advice to senior executives
  • Exceptional analytical skills with the ability to translate complex financial information into actionable insights
  • Outstanding stakeholder engagement and influencing capabilities
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills
  • Experience leading and developing high-performing teams
  • A proactive, solutions-focused approach with the ability to manage competing priorities
Applicants must be able to obtain and maintain a Negative Vetting 1 (NV1) Security Clearance.

Apply Now If you are an accomplished finance leader looking to play a key role in delivering strategic outcomes within a complex government environment, we encourage you to apply today.

job.title: DS Associate
job.description:
Warehouse Worker with Amazon
  • Work at Amazon Australia’s Delivery Station located in Cavan
  • Employee parking available onsite
  • Training and ongoing support provided
  • Flexible work with variable shift length of 4-10 hours
  • Shifts are commencing at 4.50AM
Your starting rate of pay is $35.14. You get paid penalties if you work afternoon, early morning or weekend shifts!

About the role
This is a casual role where you will be required to be available across 5 - 6 days per week (including 1 day on the weekend). We have day and night shifts available with each shift being 4-10 hours long and weekly hours averaging between 15 - 40hrs per week. Experience is not required for these positions and full training is provided, however, an ability to follow instructions and standard processes is a must.

Responsibilities
  • Sorting & labeling of parcels and boxes being sent to and from the warehouse
  • Storing/stowing received parcels and boxes throughout the facility
  • Picking parcels and boxes from shelves using an RF scanner (training provided)
  • Organising and dispatching parcels and boxes that will be sent to the customer
  • Cleaning and organisation of the site environment
  • Adhering to safety, quality and production standards
  • Standing and walking for extended periods
  • Lifting and moving products up to 23kg in weight

Successful applicants will be employed by Chandler Macleod to carry out a temporary work assignment to Amazon and will be required to complete background and police check and a drug and alcohol test. You must also have the right to work in Australia.

About Amazon
Amazon is a company with 20+ years of operational expertise and technology advancements, where the future of retail and logistics is becoming reality. Your role is key in enabling everyday deliveries for customers and being on the front line of fulfilling Amazon’s customer promise. In return Amazon offers a safe, inclusive and fun environment to set you up for success so you can work hard, have fun and make history. job.title: Maintenance Fabricator
job.description:
Maintenance Fabricator (Boilermaker) 

Chandler Macleod are seeking an experienced Maintenance Fabricator / Boilermaker for an urgent, on-site temporary assignment based in Salisbury. You’ll be supporting site operations with a strong focus on maintenance fabrication, welding repairs, and breakdown support to minimise downtime across production equipment and plant.

Key responsibilities
  • Read and interpret engineering drawings, blueprints, and measurements to ensure accurate fabrication and installation.
  • Fabricate, assemble, modify, and repair a variety of metal components, structures, frames, and safety guards.
  • Carry out MIG and TIG welding, along with general metal fabrication duties.
  • Cut, grind, drill, bend, and shape steel and other metals using a range of hand and power tools.
  • Safely operate workshop machinery and equipment, including saws, grinders, drills, presses, and welding tools.
  • Perform maintenance and repair work on machinery, conveyors, and production equipment.
  • Manufacture and modify guards, brackets, platforms, chutes, and other site-specific components.
  • Support maintenance teams during equipment breakdowns and urgent repair tasks.
  • Maintain a strong commitment to workplace health and safety, including PPE compliance and housekeeping standards.
  • Conduct quality checks on completed work to ensure it meets specifications and industry standards.
  • Undertake occasional work at heights or in confined spaces when appropriately trained and authorised.
What you’ll need
  • Trade qualification as a Boilermaker / Fabricator 
  • Solid MIG/TIG welding capability and fabrication experience in a maintenance environment
  • Ability to interpret drawings and measure/mark out accurately
  • Strong safety mindset and ability to follow site procedures
  • Availability to commit to the assignment dates and full-time hours
What’s on offer
  • Immediate start upcoming 
  • Full-time hours on a stable short-term assignment
Apply now If you’re a reliable maintenance fabricator ready to hit the ground running in Salisbury, we’d like to hear from you. Apply today and we’ll be in touch ASAP.

job.title: Senior Electrical Engineer
job.description:
Electrical Engineer | Power Generation | 6-Month Contract

Fortnightly RDO | Pinjar Power Station

Are you an experienced Electrical Engineer looking for an opportunity to contribute to Western Australia's energy infrastructure? Join the Thermal Generation team at Pinjar Power Station and play a key role in supporting critical power generation assets through engineering excellence, technical problem-solving, and project delivery.
This is a 6-month contract opportunity offering competitive hourly rates, flexible roster arrangements, and the chance to work within a highly skilled operational environment.
 
The Opportunity

As an Electrical Engineer, you will provide technical and project support to the gas turbine and distributed generation operations. You will lead engineering investigations, develop practical and innovative solutions, and contribute to the safe, reliable, and efficient operation of key generation assets.
Working within the Thermal Generation team, you will undertake a broad range of engineering assignments including project management, design services, technical assessments, conceptual proposals, and cost estimates.
 
Key Responsibilities
  • Deliver engineering support across power generation and operational assets.
  • Manage engineering projects from concept through to completion.
  • Prepare technical designs, reports, specifications, and cost estimates.
  • Lead investigations into technical and operational issues and develop practical solutions.
  • Provide expert advice on electrical plant performance, reliability, and maintenance strategies.
  • Support the ongoing safe, reliable, and efficient operation of gas turbines and distributed generation assets.
  • Liaise with internal stakeholders, contractors, and technical specialists to achieve project objectives.
 
About You

To be successful in this role, you will demonstrate:
  • A recognised Electrical Engineering qualification.
  • Approximately 5-7 years of relevant engineering experience.
  • Strong technical knowledge of:
    • Generators
    • Transformers
    • Circuit breakers
  • Experience within power generation, utilities, heavy industry, or similar operational environments.
  • Exposure to gas turbine generation assets will be highly regarded.
  • Demonstrated capability in technical investigations, engineering design, and project delivery.
  • Strong problem-solving, communication, and stakeholder management skills.
 
What's on Offer?
✅ 6-month contract with an immediate start available
✅ 75 hours per fortnight
✅ Fortnightly RDO roster with flexibility to choose your RDO day within the fortnight
✅ Opportunity to work at a critical generation facility supporting WA's energy network
✅ Collaborative and safety-focused team environment
 

Additional Requirements
As this position is classified as a Security of Critical Infrastructure (SoCI) critical role, successful applicants will be required to complete and pass an AusCheck background screening process before commencement.
 
If you're an experienced Electrical Engineer with a strong background in power generation and a passion for delivering practical engineering solutions, we'd love to hear from you.
Submit your application today and contribute to the safe and reliable operation of one of Western Australia's key power generation facilities.

job.title: Continuous Improvement/Operations Lead
job.description:
Continuous Improvement/Operations LeadLocation: Port Macquarie
Term: 6 months (TBC)
Reporting to: Head of People & Culture

The Role
We're looking for a hands-on Continuous Improvement or Operations Lead to help improve how work gets done across a division of the organisation. This is a practical, delivery-focused role for someone who can identify improvement opportunities, bring people together, create structure where it's needed, and drive initiatives through to implementation.
The role will focus on improving operational effectiveness, aligning processes across teams, creating consistency in ways of working, and ensuring business initiatives deliver measurable outcomes. Working across multiple functions, you'll collaborate with a wide range of stakeholders, with the Head of People & Culture acting as the key sponsor.

Key Responsibilities
  • Lead and coordinate change, improvement and operational initiatives across the business.
  • Identify opportunities to streamline processes, improve efficiency and enhance ways of working.
  • Drive continuous improvement projects from concept through to implementation and adoption.
  • Review, align and standardise processes to create consistency across teams and functions.
  • Develop and document processes, procedures, workflows and SOPs.
  • Leverage AI and technology tools to improve productivity, documentation and operational effectiveness.
  • Facilitate workshops, project meetings and stakeholder forums to drive outcomes and accountability.
  • Establish project plans, timelines, actions and governance to ensure successful delivery.
  • Monitor progress, remove roadblocks and ensure initiatives achieve intended business outcomes.
  • Build strong relationships across the organisation and support people through change.
About You

You need to be someone with good energy, take initiative and who gets stuff done. You're naturally curious, enjoy solving problems, and don't wait for perfect information before getting started. Curious, practical and comfortable working things out rather than waiting for a perfect brief.
You'll bring:
  • Strong stakeholder engagement, influencing and communication skills.
  • Experience leading business improvement, change or transformation initiatives.
  • The ability to create structure, clarity and accountability in fast-moving environments.
  • Excellent organisational and project coordination skills.
  • Confidence facilitating meetings and driving outcomes.
  • A practical, solutions-focused mindset.
  • Strong process improvement and documentation capability.
  • An interest in AI, technology and innovative ways of working.
  • Flexibility and adaptability when priorities shift.
  • A continuous improvement mindset and desire to make things work better.
In a Nutshell

This is an opportunity for a practical improvement leader who can step into a business, assess what's working and what isn't, align processes, create structure, engage stakeholders, and drive meaningful change. You'll combine project delivery, operational improvement and change management capabilities to ensure initiatives are not only designed well, but successfully implemented and embedded.

For any questions or a confidential conversation, call Jo on 02 6691 9106 or Mary or 02 6691 9102

job.title: Picker Loader - Distribution
job.description:
Passionate about producing premium quality poultry products through the Lilydale Free Range and Steggles brands, Baiada has been bringing Australian families together at the dinner table since 1919.

Supplying fresh poultry to retailers nationwide and value-added products to Quick Service Restaurants and food service customers, Baiada is an industry leader known for innovation, efficiency, and its commitment to delivering high-quality products every day.

As a Picker Loader / Forklift Operator within the Distribution team, you will play an important role in ensuring customer orders are accurately picked, handled, and dispatched safely and on time. This is a day shift position working from 7:00am, with full-time hours available.

Your responsibilities will include:

  • Operating forklifts safely and efficiently within the distribution area
  • Picking, scanning, and preparing customer orders for dispatch
  • Loading and unloading trucks in accordance with site procedures
  • Handling raw chicken products and maintaining product quality standards
  • Working in chilled and cold storage environments
  • Conducting pre-start forklift inspections and reporting any issues
  • Ensuring stock is stored, rotated, and managed correctly
  • Maintaining accurate inventory and dispatch records
  • Maintaining a clean, safe, and organised work area
  • Following all food safety, quality, and WHS requirements
  • Assisting with general warehouse and distribution duties as required
About You To be successful in this role, you will bring:

  • Current and valid LF Forklift Licence
  • Previous experience operating a forklift in a warehouse or distribution environment
  • Ability to perform manual handling tasks and work with raw poultry products
  • Comfortable working in a cold environment
  • Strong attention to detail and accuracy when picking orders
  • Good communication and teamwork skills
  • Commitment to workplace safety and following procedures
  • Reliable attendance and a strong work ethic
  • Flexibility to work overtime when required
  • Ability to work in a fast-paced environment and meet daily operational targets
Click APPLY NOW or contact the Baiada Recruitment Team on 02 6762 9055 or email baiadahanwood@chandlermacleod.com for a confidential discussion regarding this opportunity.

job.title: Project Engineer - Electrical
job.description:
Project Engineer - Electrical

Location: Brisbane CBD
Roster: Monday to Friday
Duration: Immediate start through to September 2027

About the Role
We are seeking an experienced Electrical Project Engineer to join a major mining and infrastructure program delivering innovative remote operations technology. This role will be responsible for leading the delivery of electrical, communications, control systems, and Operational Technology (OT) infrastructure projects that support the rollout of Remote Control Dozer operations across multiple sites.
Working within a multidisciplinary project team, you will oversee the design, construction, commissioning, and handover of remote operations control rooms and associated infrastructure, ensuring projects are delivered safely, on schedule, and within budget.

Key Responsibilities
  • Lead the end-to-end delivery of electrical infrastructure and remote operations projects.
  • Manage the development and execution of stockpile remote operations control rooms.
  • Coordinate electrical, communications, networking, OT, and control systems interfaces.
  • Manage engineering consultants, contractors, vendors, and project budgets.
  • Ensure compliance with site safety requirements, engineering standards, and project governance processes.
  • Support commissioning, operational readiness activities, training, and project handover.
  • Engage with key stakeholders across operations, maintenance, technology, and project teams to achieve successful project outcomes.
About You
  • Degree qualification in Electrical Engineering, or an electrical trade background with demonstrated project delivery experience.
  • Proven experience delivering electrical infrastructure or capital projects within mining, resources, or heavy industry environments.
  • Strong project management, contractor management, and stakeholder engagement skills.
  • Ability to manage multiple workstreams and coordinate multidisciplinary teams.
  • Experience with remote operations, communications networks, automation, control systems, or Operational Technology (OT) will be highly regarded.
What's on Offer
  • Long-term contract through to September 2027.
  • Brisbane CBD based role with a Monday to Friday roster.
  • Opportunity to contribute to cutting-edge remote operations and automation projects.
  • Work within a high-performing team delivering strategically important infrastructure projects.
If you're an experienced Electrical Project Engineer looking to play a key role in the future of mining technology and remote operations, we'd love to hear from you.

job.title: Internal Audit
job.description:
Chandler Macleod is recruiting on behalf of our Federal Government client for an experienced Audit and Assurance Officer to join their Governance team in Albury NSW, Griffith NSW,  Canberra ACT, Goondiwindi QLD, Mildura VIC, Adelaide SA , Murray Bridge SA. This is a 12 month, full time labour hire contract.
This is an excellent opportunity for a governance, audit, risk, or assurance professional to contribute to the delivery of effective governance frameworks, organisational resilience, risk management, and continuous improvement initiatives within a high-profile Commonwealth agency.

About the Role
The Audit and Assurance Officer plays a key role in supporting the agency's governance, audit, assurance, risk management, and business continuity functions.
Working closely with internal stakeholders, service providers, and governance committees, you will coordinate internal audits, monitor audit recommendations, support risk and assurance activities, and contribute to the ongoing improvement of governance and risk frameworks. You will also assist in strengthening organisational resilience through the management and coordination of business continuity planning and testing activities.

Key Responsibilities
As the Audit and Assurance Officer, you will:
  • Manage relationships and contracts with internal audit service providers, ensuring accountability and delivery against agreed milestones.
  • Coordinate the delivery of internal audits in accordance with the Annual Internal Audit Plan.
  • Liaise with stakeholders, facilitate information gathering, track audit progress, and support audit activities from commencement through to completion.
  • Maintain audit recommendation registers and monitor the implementation, reporting, escalation, and closure of management actions.
  • Prepare high-quality reports, briefings, and committee papers relating to audit, assurance, risk management, and business continuity matters.
  • Contribute to the continuous improvement of governance, audit, assurance, and risk management frameworks.
  • Coordinate quality assurance activities and support annual assessments of internal audit service effectiveness.
  • Support the effective operation of governance and oversight committees, including member onboarding and administrative coordination.
  • Coordinate external reviews, assurance activities, compliance assessments, and risk workshops.
  • Manage and maintain business continuity arrangements, including planning, testing exercises, resilience initiatives, and monitoring improvement actions.
  • Provide specialist advice on governance, audit, assurance, risk, and business continuity matters across the organisation.
About You
To be successful in this role, you will have demonstrated experience in governance, audit, assurance, risk management, compliance, or related fields within a government or highly regulated environment.

You will bring:
Audit, Risk & Assurance Expertise
  • Experience coordinating internal audit programs and assurance activities.
  • Strong understanding of governance, risk management, and control frameworks.
  • Knowledge of Australian Government audit, risk, and assurance principles.
  • Experience managing audit findings, recommendations, and reporting processes.
  • Understanding of business continuity planning and organisational resilience practices.
Strategic Thinking & Analysis
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills.
  • Ability to interpret complex information, identify emerging trends, and recommend practical improvements.
  • Experience contributing to strategic planning and assurance priorities.
  • Understanding of performance metrics, data analysis, and reporting.
Communication & Stakeholder Engagement
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
  • Experience preparing executive-level reports, briefing papers, and committee documentation.
  • Ability to influence, negotiate, and build credibility with senior stakeholders.
  • Strong relationship management and contract management capabilities.
Personal Effectiveness
  • Ability to work independently while collaborating effectively across geographically dispersed teams.
  • Strong organisational skills with the ability to manage competing priorities and meet deadlines.
  • High attention to detail and commitment to quality outcomes.
  • Sound judgement and the ability to provide trusted advice on complex governance and assurance matters.
 
Apply Now

job.title: Data Engineer
job.description:
Data Engineer - Asset Management & Transformation

  • Opportunity with Rio Tinto
  • $105 - $110 per hour + 12% superannuation
  • Monday to Friday
  • CBD - Central Park
  • 6-month assignment via Chandler Macleod
  • Support major asset management and operational improvement initiatives

About the Opportunity

Rio Tinto is a global mining and materials company, focused on finding, mining and processing the resources the world needs. Through Chandler Macleod's partnership with Rio Tinto, we are seeking experienced Data Analysts to support several business-critical transformation initiatives across Iron Ore operations.

Working within a collaborative Improvement & Technology environment, you will help drive better asset management outcomes through data-driven insights and analytics. The role will focus on analysing operational and maintenance data, identifying improvement opportunities, and supporting initiatives that improve equipment reliability, reduce waste, and optimise maintenance performance.

This position would suit someone with experience working with asset management, maintenance, reliability, mining, resources, manufacturing, or heavy industry datasets who enjoys turning complex information into actionable business insights.

Reporting to the Principal Asset, Data & Systems and working closely with operational stakeholders, you will:

  • Analyse asset management and maintenance datasets to identify trends, opportunities, and performance improvements
  • Develop and maintain Power BI dashboards and reporting solutions
  • Extract, transform, and analyse data using SQL
  • Work with SAP asset management and maintenance data to support business decision-making
  • Support initiatives focused on reducing tool time for fixed plant and mobile equipment maintenance activities
  • Analyse inventory and spare parts data to identify wastage reduction opportunities
  • Provide insights to improve asset health, equipment reliability, and maintenance effectiveness
  • Collaborate with operational, maintenance, and asset management stakeholders to understand business requirements
  • Support the delivery of transformation and continuous improvement projects across Iron Ore operations
  • Ensure data quality, governance, and reporting standards are maintained

About You
  • Experience working with asset management, maintenance, reliability, operational, or business performance data
  • Advanced Power BI reporting and dashboard development skills
  • Strong SQL querying and data analysis experience
  • Experience working with SAP data, ideally within asset management or maintenance environments
  • Knowledge of database structures and data management principles
  • Ability to communicate insights to both technical and non-technical stakeholders
  • Strong problem-solving and analytical thinking skills
  • Experience within mining, resources, heavy industry, utilities, manufacturing, or similar operational environments

Highly Regarded
  • Exposure to Databricks environments
  • Experience with Python, R, or other programming languages
  • Understanding of maintenance, reliability, and asset management principles
  • Previous involvement in business transformation or continuous improvement initiatives

Why Join Chandler Macleod?

Chandler Macleod is one of Australia's leading workforce solutions providers. You'll receive competitive pay rates paid weekly, superannuation on all hours worked, access to our Employee Assistance Program, ongoing support from a dedicated Chandler Macleod consultant, streamlined digital onboarding, and opportunities to work on future Rio Tinto assignments.

job.title: Senior Town Planner
job.description:
Senior Town Planner
Location: Charlestown, NSW
Work Type: Full-time | Flexible working

Our client is seeking an experienced Senior Town Planner to join a well-established consultancy delivering a diverse range of planning and development projects across NSW.

job.title: Senior Project Manager (Civil Construction)
job.description:
Permanent | Cairns | Senior Project Leadership | Civil Construction


For an experienced civil Project Manager, this is an opportunity to take genuine ownership of project delivery, with responsibility extending well beyond programme management and reporting.

Based in Cairns, this permanent Senior Project Manager position sits within an established civil construction business delivering a diverse range of infrastructure projects.

This isn't a role sitting several layers removed from construction. You'll have overall responsibility for the project and its performance, leading the delivery team while maintaining oversight across commercial, programme, quality, safety, client and construction outcomes.

You'll be supported by an experienced engineering and quality team, including Project Engineers, Site Engineers and quality resources. The expectation is that you'll provide the leadership, direction and commercial oversight needed to keep projects performing from mobilisation through to completion.


What you'll be responsible for:


Your remit will cover the full lifecycle of civil construction projects, including:
  • Taking overall responsibility for project delivery from mobilisation through to completion
  • Leading Project Engineers, Site Engineers, supervisors, subcontractors and project support resources
  • Managing project budgets, forecasting, cost performance and overall commercial outcomes
  • Developing and driving construction programmes and ensuring key milestones are achieved
  • Managing procurement, subcontractors, variations and contractual requirements
  • Maintaining strong standards across safety, quality, compliance and project risk
  • Building effective relationships with clients, stakeholders and delivery partners
  • Providing practical leadership and direction to resolve issues and keep projects moving
  • Taking accountability for the performance of both the project and the team delivering it

Who we're looking for:


We're looking for someone who has built their career close to civil construction delivery and understands what it means to have genuine accountability for the whole project.

This will particularly suit someone experienced in a regional or mid-sized civil contractor environment, where Project Managers are expected to understand the commercial detail, know what's happening on site, lead their teams and take ownership of the final outcome.


To be considered, you'll need to bring:
  • A Degree in Civil Engineering (highly regarded)
  • Substantial experience in civil construction, with ideally five or more years operating at Project Manager level
  • A strong contractor-side background delivering civil infrastructure projects
  • Demonstrated experience taking projects from planning and mobilisation through construction to completion
  • Strong commercial capability across budgets, forecasting, procurement, contracts and cost control
  • Experience leading engineering, construction and subcontractor teams
  • A practical understanding of civil construction methodology, quality, safety and project risk
  • The judgement and leadership capability to make decisions, solve problems and remain accountable for project outcomes


Why consider the opportunity?


If you're looking for a role where you can have genuine influence over how projects are run, this is an opportunity to take ownership without being lost within a large corporate project structure.
You'll be close enough to the work to understand what's happening on site while having the autonomy and support to lead the broader project, team and commercial outcomes.


The opportunity offers:
  • A permanent Senior Project Manager position based in Cairns
  • Genuine end-to-end ownership of civil construction projects
  • Dedicated engineering and quality support
  • A hands-on leadership role with direct influence over project performance
  • An established civil construction environment where experienced Project Managers are trusted to lead
  • Exposure to a diverse range of civil infrastructure projects
This could particularly suit an experienced Senior Project Manager or Project Manager who has built a career within civil contracting and is ready for broader responsibility across projects, people and commercial performance.


If your experience aligns and you'd like a confidential discussion about the position, projects, package and opportunity to establish yourself in Cairns, apply now or contact Anna Dziopa at Chandler Macleod on 07 2140 6649.

  • Support governance, planning and stakeholder engagement activities across Army Headquarters.
  • Assist in translating complex technical and military information into clear strategic advice.
  • Contribute to capability lifecycle planning, investment decisions and future force design initiatives.

You Must Have
  • Demonstrated experience supporting Defence programs, force design, capability development or strategic planning activities.
  • Strong understanding of Defence capability, communications systems, information systems, or integrated capability environments.
  • Excellent written communication skills, including experience preparing strategic documents, reports and briefings.

job.title: Senior Lead Data Analyst
job.description:
About the company:

This Federal Government agency works to deliver programs and services that support people with disability and their families, aiming to improve access, engagement, and outcomes across Australia. The agency collaborates closely with communities, service providers, and government stakeholders to implement initiatives that enhance social inclusion, wellbeing, and equity.

About the Team

The team plays a critical role in supporting the agency's risk and integrity functions through advanced data analysis, reporting, and evidence-based insights. Working in a highly collaborative environment, the team partners with stakeholders across business areas to identify trends, manage risks, improve decision-making, and support strategic priorities. job.title: Transfer Station Operator
job.description:
About the role
We’re seeking a reliable Transfer Station Operator to support day-to-day operations at a busy Resource Recovery/Waste Management Centre in Ballina. You’ll be the first point of contact for visitors, providing helpful, calm customer service while directing vehicles and customers to the correct drop-off areas and encouraging safe, compliant recycling and resource recovery. The role also includes hands-on site support such as general labouring and grounds maintenance (e.g., litter collection, mowing/weeding and basic upkeep), completing standard paperwork (timesheets, work orders and WHS documentation), and working safely in line with site procedures.

Working hours are a key part of this role: you’ll work 7:30am–4:30pm on a rotating roster, starting 2–3 days per week with the potential to increase to full-time hours in early 2027. You must be available Monday to Friday and also commit to at least one weekend day (Saturday or Sunday) per fortnight—regular weekend work is required.


Duties
  • Provide friendly, professional customer service to waste centre visitors
  • Direct traffic and customers to the correct drop-off areas
  • Promote resource recovery and recycling by guiding correct sorting
  • Communicate load contents and details to the weighbridge operator
  • Advise customers on accepted vs non-accepted waste materials
  • Complete physically demanding outdoor work while following site safety requirements

Skills and Experience
  • Strong customer service and communication skills (confident dealing with the public)
  • Previous experience in physical, hands-on labouring work
  • Ability to follow procedures and communicate requirements clearly to customers
  • Strong work ethic, reliability, and initiative
  • Hepatitis A and B immunisation (required , or willingness to obtain)

Desirable:
  • Forklift ticket and practical operating experience
  • Waste management / transfer station / resource recovery experience
  • FEL tickets & white card 

Benefits
  • Strong weekend rates (Saturday $49 + super and Sunday $63 + super)
  • Consistent daytime hours (7:30am–4:30pm)
  • Opportunity to increase to full-time hours in early 2027 (performance and site needs dependent)

How to apply
Sound interesting? We would love to hear from you! Click APPLY NOW to upload a copy of your current resume & cover letter, or call Neva Niland on 02 6691 9101  for a confidential discussion.

Our client is a well-established and growing Australian business supplying premium aluminium façade and architectural systems to the construction industry. Due to continued growth, they are seeking an ambitious Business Development Manager to drive sales, expand market share, and contribute to their long-term success.

Location Shepparton, VIC

Employment Type Full-Time, Permanent

About the Opportunity Reporting into the leadership team, you will be responsible for identifying and developing new business opportunities, managing an existing sales pipeline, and building strong relationships across the construction sector.

The successful candidate will play a key role in growing market presence and securing project specifications with architects and builders throughout a designated territory.

With a healthy pipeline of active and pending projects already in place, you'll be responsible for maintaining momentum, converting opportunities into sales, and expanding business growth.

Key Responsibilities
  • Develop and maintain relationships with architects, builders, developers, and contractors.
  • Secure project specifications and manage opportunities through the full sales cycle.
  • Maintain and grow a strong pipeline of sales opportunities.
  • Conduct regular client meetings and site visits across your territory.
  • Collaborate with estimating and marketing teams to generate quality leads.
  • Utilise CRM systems to manage opportunities, record activity, and track performance.
  • Monitor and maintain pipeline accuracy and reporting.
  • Work closely with internal stakeholders to achieve sales and growth targets.
  • Stay informed on construction industry trends, façade systems, and architectural products.
  • Deliver exceptional customer service and contribute to long-term client retention.
About You We're looking for someone who is commercially minded, self-motivated, and passionate about sales.

Essential Requirements
  • Minimum 2 years' experience selling construction materials in a B2B environment.
  • Proven experience dealing with architects, builders, and construction stakeholders.
  • Strong understanding of the construction industry.
  • Experience using CRM systems and working to weekly KPIs.
  • Demonstrated ability to manage a sales pipeline and drive results.
  • Excellent communication, negotiation, and relationship-building skills.
  • Highly motivated, resilient, and target-driven.
  • Willingness to undertake administrative tasks as part of a small and agile team environment.
  • Current driver's licence.
Desirable Qualifications & Experience
  • Qualifications in Building Design, Architecture, Construction Management, or a related field.
  • Experience with architectural façade systems or building products.
  • Ability to read and interpret construction drawings.
  • Experience with specification sales.
What We're Looking For The ideal candidate will embody the qualities of being:

  • Hungry – driven to succeed and exceed targets.

  • Smart – commercially aware with strong interpersonal skills.
You'll be someone who enjoys building relationships, creating opportunities, and taking ownership of your results.

Salary & Benefits
  • Base salary of $110,000 + Super
  • Uncapped commission and bonus structure
  • Laptop and mobile phone provided
  • Opportunity to work with an established and growing business
  • Long-term career development potential
  • Autonomy and flexibility in managing your territory

Apply today or contact Chandler Macleod for a confidential discussion.

job.title: Senior Cyber Security Advisor
job.description:
Are you an experienced Cyber Security professional with a strong advisory background and expertise supporting complex, highly regulated environments?

We are seeking a Senior Cyber Security Advisor to join our client AGL on a contract basis. This is a strategic role responsible for providing expert cyber security guidance across business and technology initiatives, helping strengthen cyber resilience and protect critical infrastructure against an evolving threat landscape. This is an initial six month contract, based in Melbourne in a hybrid working environment.

Working closely with senior stakeholders across business and technology teams, you will play a key role in identifying, assessing and managing cyber security risks while ensuring compliance with industry standards, regulatory requirements and organisational policies.

About the Role

As a trusted cyber security partner, you will provide strategic advice and leadership across a broad range of initiatives, ensuring security considerations are embedded into decision-making, transformation programs and operational activities.

Key responsibilities include:
  • Provide expert cyber security advice across strategic and operational initiatives.
  • Identify, assess and manage cyber security risks across technology and business projects.
  • Partner with business leaders, technology teams, subsidiaries, vendors and external stakeholders to strengthen cyber security outcomes.
  • Develop, implement and maintain cyber security policies, standards and guidelines.
  • Ensure alignment with relevant cyber security regulations, legislation and industry frameworks.
  • Communicate cyber security risks, priorities and technical debt to executive and business leadership teams.
  • Deliver cyber security awareness activities, workshops and mentoring sessions for technical and non-technical stakeholders.
  • Support compliance initiatives and drive improvements in security posture across IT and Operational Technology (OT) environments.
  • Develop reporting and metrics to measure cyber security maturity and effectiveness.
  • Act as a senior point of escalation and provide leadership support when required.
About You

To be successful in this role, you will bring strong cyber security advisory experience, excellent stakeholder engagement skills and the ability to translate complex technical concepts into practical business outcomes.

You will ideally have:
  • Demonstrated experience leading cyber security advisory and consulting engagements within Public Sector and/or Government environments.
  • Proven experience across Cyber Security, IT/OT Security, Technology Risk or Information Security.
  • Strong understanding of Australian cyber security legislation and regulatory requirements, including the Security of Critical Infrastructure (SoCI) Act and Privacy Act.
  • Experience working with recognised industry frameworks and standards such as:
    • NIST Cyber Security Framework (CSF)
    • ISA/IEC 62443
    • MITRE ATT&CK
    • D3FEND
    • Australian Energy Sector Cyber Security Framework (AESCSF)
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to influence stakeholders at all levels.
  • Strong programme and project delivery experience.
  • Proven ability to communicate complex cyber risks in clear business language.
  • Experience in risk management, governance and compliance environment.

If you're a seasoned Cyber Security professional looking to make an impact within a complex and critical environment, we'd love to hear from you.

Apply now to be considered.

You can read more about our commitment to diversity and inclusion at https://www.chandlermacleod.com/diversity-and-inclusion.

job.title: Technical Sales Manager
job.description:
Kalgoorlie, WA | Residential Role | Company Vehicle | Relocation Support

Are you an experienced mining professional with a strong background in ESCO Ground Engaging Tools (GET), buckets, lips and wear components?

Have you worked in Kalgoorlie and developed strong site-level relationships across the Goldfields?

This is an outstanding opportunity to join a global leader in mining technology and wear solutions, taking ownership of key customer relationships and supporting some of Western Australia's most significant surface mining operations.

This is a residential Kalgoorlie position. FIFO applications will not be considered.

About the Opportunity
As the company's on-site ESCO representative, you will be responsible for supporting existing customers, monitoring product performance, identifying growth opportunities and defending market share across a portfolio of large mining operations throughout the Goldfields region.

You will become the trusted technical advisor for customers, providing expert guidance on ESCO wear products, conducting inspections, delivering performance reports and identifying opportunities to improve productivity and reduce operating costs.

Success in this role will come from your ability to build strong site relationships, understand mining operations, and leverage your existing Goldfields network to influence decisions and drive commercial outcomes.

What We're Looking For To be successful, you will ideally bring:
  • Previous hands-on experience with ESCO products, GET systems, buckets, lips and wear components
  • Strong understanding of surface mining operations and heavy mobile equipment
  • Existing relationships and networks across Kalgoorlie and Goldfields mine sites
  • Demonstrated experience conducting bucket inspections, wear analysis and product performance reporting
  • Ability to identify opportunities for product conversions and market share growth
  • Strong customer engagement and stakeholder management skills
  • Experience working directly with maintenance, reliability, planning and operational teams
  • Salesforce CRM experience highly regarded
  • Current driver's licence
Essential Requirements
  • Minimum 5 years' experience within the mining industry
  • Previous experience in a technical, product support, field service or mining sales support role
  • Existing knowledge of ESCO products and applications
  • Prior work history in the Kalgoorlie region with established site contacts and industry networks
  • Ability to travel regularly across customer operations throughout the Goldfields
What's On Offer
  • Highly competitive salary package
  • Fully maintained company vehicle
  • Four weeks' temporary accommodation assistance
  • Long-term career opportunity with a global industry leader
  • Autonomy to manage key accounts and customer relationships
  • Exposure to major mining operations and decision-makers
  • Opportunity to influence product performance, market growth and customer outcomes
Why Apply?

This role is not suited to someone looking to learn ESCO products from scratch.

We are seeking a proven mining industry professional who already understands ESCO applications, has credibility on mine sites, and can leverage established relationships across the Kalgoorlie region to immediately add value.

If you have the technical expertise, commercial mindset and Goldfields network to become a trusted advisor to mining customers, we would welcome your application.

About the company:

The team plays a critical role in supporting the agency's risk and integrity functions through advanced data analysis, reporting, and evidence-based insights. Working in a highly collaborative environment, the team partners with stakeholders across business areas to identify trends, manage risks, improve decision-making, and support strategic priorities. Team members contribute to complex projects that help drive operational excellence and deliver meaningful outcomes for Australians.

An exciting opportunity exists for an experienced Data Analyst to join the agency. This role requires a highly capable professional who can work independently on complex analytical activities, provide strategic insights, and support decision-making through data-driven recommendations.
The successful candidate will undertake detailed analytical work, manage competing priorities, and contribute to projects that influence both operational and strategic outcomes. You will collaborate with a wide range of stakeholders, present findings to diverse audiences, and provide guidance to junior team members.
This is an excellent opportunity for someone who enjoys solving complex problems, working with large datasets, and translating data into meaningful insights that drive organisational outcomes.


Key Responsibilities
  • Conduct complex data analysis, reporting, and investigative activities to support business objectives.
  • Manage day-to-day analytical tasks, including regular reporting, project work, and ad hoc requests.
  • Analyse large and complex datasets to identify trends, risks, opportunities, and business insights.
  • Develop and maintain reports, dashboards, and performance metrics.
  • Contribute to reporting governance, quality assurance, and data integrity processes.
  • Interpret analytical findings and provide evidence-based recommendations to stakeholders.

  • Present analytical outcomes and insights to both technical and non-technical audiences.
  • Support stakeholder engagement and build strong internal and external relationships.
  • Mentor and develop junior analysts, promoting best practices in data analysis and reporting.
  • Support project delivery and contribute to strategic initiatives within the risk and integrity functions.

You Must Have
 
  • Strong experience in data analytics and data interpretation.
  • Advanced SQL skills and experience working with large datasets.
  • Experience using analytics and reporting tools, ideally SAS Enterprise Guide (SAS EG) and/or SAS Viya.
  • Strong problem-solving skills with the ability to identify and resolve complex data-related issues.
  • Excellent critical thinking capabilities and the ability to make evidence-based decisions.
  • Strong communication skills, including the ability to explain complex data insights to both technical and non-technical audiences.
  • Proven ability to build productive stakeholder relationships and collaborate across multidisciplinary teams.
  • Experience preparing reports, presentations, and briefing materials for senior stakeholders.
  • Ability to manage multiple priorities and work effectively with a high degree of autonomy.
  • Experience with Python and/or R programming languages.
  • Knowledge of statistical analysis and machine learning techniques.
  • Experience in fraud analytics, risk analytics, or integrity-related environments.
  • Experience working within a large and complex government or regulated environment.


Benefits:
  • ASAP start (pending Federal Police Clearance)
  • 12-month assignment with potential extension
  • Location:  Deakin ACT, Richmond VIC, Geelong VIC, Chermside QLD, Surry Hills NSW, Newcastle NSW

Chandler Macleod is an equal opportunity employer as part of our commitment to creating a diverse and inclusive workplace, Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people, disability and culturally and linguistics candidates are also encouraged to apply.

This is an opportunity to influence direction, lead meaningful change, and deliver environmental and sustainability outcomes that will have a lasting impact on a rapidly growing community.
We are seeking an experienced and forward-thinking leader to oversee a diverse Environment and Sustainability portfolio. This senior position spans environmental management and compliance, sustainability strategy, climate and carbon initiatives, circular economy programs, waste and resource recovery planning, stakeholder engagement, and strategic partnerships.
The portfolio is broad and varied, bringing together environmental stewardship, sustainability leadership, operational planning, regulatory responsibilities, and community-focused outcomes.
While waste and resource recovery form an important component of the role, the primary focus is leading a high-performing Environment and Sustainability function that can respond to growth, meet legislative obligations, and deliver practical, measurable results.
Candidates may come from local government, state government, environmental management, sustainability, consulting, infrastructure, utilities, resources, or other highly regulated sectors. More important than sector background is the ability to lead people, navigate complexity, make sound decisions, and turn strategic objectives into action.

Why this opportunity matters

Population growth brings significant environmental, operational, and community challenges.
This role will play a critical part in shaping how the organisation responds to those challenges, balancing environmental protection, compliance, sustainability priorities, resource recovery, and community expectations.

Reporting to the Executive Director Technical Services, you will lead a multidisciplinary team responsible for strategic planning, service delivery, compliance, stakeholder engagement, and operational outcomes.

You will have the opportunity to:
  • Lead the organisation's environmental and sustainability agenda.
  • Drive initiatives across environmental planning, compliance, sustainability, circular economy, carbon reduction, and waste management.
  • Create focus, alignment, and momentum across a complex portfolio.
  • Develop team capability and foster a culture of accountability and continuous improvement.
  • Provide high-quality advice to executives, elected members, and internal stakeholders.
  • Strengthen partnerships with government agencies, industry bodies, community organisations, and regional collaborators.
  • Secure funding opportunities and establish strategic partnerships that deliver long-term community and environmental benefits.
Who we're looking for

This role will suit a leader who enjoys solving problems, making decisions, and delivering outcomes in dynamic and evolving environments.
You may have gained your experience in environmental management, sustainability, consulting, infrastructure, utilities, waste management, resources, local government, state government, or another complex operational setting.
You may not have held the title of Head of Environment and Sustainability before, but you will possess the leadership capability, professional judgement, and credibility required to lead a significant and diverse function.

To be successful, you will bring:
  • Demonstrated leadership experience within environmental, sustainability, or related service areas.
  • A proactive and solutions-focused leadership approach.
  • The confidence to take ownership, make decisions, and deliver results.
  • Strong knowledge of environmental compliance, governance, risk management, and regulatory frameworks.
  • The ability to operate effectively across technical, operational, community, and political environments.
  • Experience leading teams through change, growth, and competing priorities.
  • Sound financial management, procurement, contract management, and project delivery skills.
  • Strong communication and influencing skills, with the ability to engage effectively at senior levels.
Above all, you will be a practical and capable leader who can assess what matters most, set a clear course of action, and deliver outcomes that make a genuine difference for the organisation and community.

job.title: Delivery project Support Officer
job.description:
About the company:

This Federal Government agency is responsible for protecting and advancing national security interests through the management of defence policy, strategy, and operations. It oversees the development and delivery of complex defence capabilities, including advanced maritime, land, and aerospace programs, while coordinating with domestic and international partners.

Delivery project Support Officer– 12-Month Assignment
Location: Canberra ACT
Security Clearance: Minimum NV1 Clearance

About the Team
Join a high-performing and integrated capability delivery team supporting the delivery of complex communications, information and technology projects within a large government agency. Working alongside Project Managers, Systems Engineers, Integration Specialists and Program Assurance professionals, you will contribute to the successful delivery of strategic capability outcomes.

The team operates in a collaborative, fast-paced environment where governance, stakeholder engagement and disciplined project delivery are critical to success. This is an excellent opportunity to work across a broad range of projects while supporting capability outcomes that have a meaningful impact.

About the Role
The Project Support Officer (PSO) is responsible for providing project coordination, governance, administration and reporting support across assigned capability streams. Reporting to the Program Delivery Lead, you will assist project teams in achieving program objectives through effective information management, stakeholder coordination and governance support.
You will play a key role in maintaining project documentation, coordinating meetings and governance activities, supporting reporting processes, and ensuring project information is managed in accordance with organisational policies and requirements.

Responsibilities

Project Coordination and Support
  • Provide day-to-day project support across multiple delivery streams.
  • Coordinate project activities, milestones, schedules and information flows.
  • Support planning, tracking and reporting of project delivery activities.
  • Assist delivery teams to meet project objectives and key milestones.

Governance and Reporting
  • Support governance, reporting and assurance activities.
  • Prepare, coordinate and maintain governance documentation and reporting artefacts.
  • Track and report risks, issues, actions, decisions and dependencies.
  • Assist in the preparation of reports, briefs, presentations and governance papers.

Documentation and Information Management
  • Maintain project records, registers and documentation in accordance with organisational policies.
  • Support document control, records management and configuration management activities.
  • Coordinate information management workflows using approved systems and tools.
  • Ensure project information remains accurate, current and accessible.

Stakeholder Coordination
  • Coordinate stakeholder inputs and consolidate information to support governance and decision-making activities.
  • Organise and support meetings, workshops, boards and working groups.
  • Prepare agendas, minutes and action registers.
  • Liaise with internal and external stakeholders to facilitate project delivery activities.
Program Support
  • Support audits, reviews and assurance activities as required.
  • Provide administrative and coordination support to project and assurance teams.
  • Contribute to continuous improvement initiatives relating to governance and project support processes.
  • Ensure activities are conducted in accordance with agency policies, governance frameworks and program requirements.

Professional Contribution
  • Operate collaboratively within an integrated delivery team.
  • Demonstrate initiative, sound judgement and professionalism.
  • Contribute to a positive, accountable and outcomes-focused team culture.


You Must Have
  • Demonstrated experience in project support, project coordination or program administration within a structured project environment.
  • Strong organisational and time-management skills with the ability to manage competing priorities.
  • Experience preparing and maintaining project documentation, registers and reporting artefacts.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills.
  • Proven ability to engage effectively with a diverse range of stakeholders.
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office applications and information management systems.
  • Ability to operate effectively in a fast-paced and evolving environment.

Desirable
  • Experience working within a government, regulated or large-scale enterprise environment.
  • Familiarity with governance frameworks, project lifecycle management and assurance processes.
  • Experience supporting multiple projects or program delivery environments.
  • Qualifications or training in Project Management, Business Administration or a related discipline.
  • Experience with information management and records management systems.
  • Exposure to communications, information technology or capability delivery projects.


How to apply:

Chandler Macleod is an equal opportunity employer as part of our commitment to creating a diverse and inclusive workplace, Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people, disability and culturally and linguistics candidates are also encouraged to apply.

Please note the successful candidate for the role must hold Australian Citizenship.

Application closes on the 5th of October 2026

job.title: Onsite Account Manager
